Quicksort, step by step

Quicksort picks a pivot, moves every smaller value to its left, puts the pivot in its final place, then sorts the two sides the same way. This version uses the Lomuto partition with the last value as the pivot.

Click the figure, then use ← →, space, Home and End, or the buttons.

How it works

  1. Take the last value in the range as the pivot.
  2. Walk the range. Each value smaller than the pivot is swapped into the left part.
  3. Swap the pivot just after the left part. It is now in its final place.
  4. Sort the part left of the pivot, then the part right of it.

Cost

Time
O(n log n) on average. O(n²) when the pivot is always the smallest or largest, such as sorted input here.
Space
O(log n) stack on average, O(n) in the worst case.
Stable
No.

The code behind this figure

Nothing here is hand-animated. The figure comes from this code: a plain quicksort with stepthru tracer calls, such as compare and swap, that record each step.
